rv.q: Whatever the show’s future, Beane and the young producing team of Broadway neophytes have made it a guilt-free pleasure to visit “a place where nobody dared to go.”
This show knows exactly what it is: a gleefully silly celebration of all that was wonderfully cheesy about the era that brought us disco balls and roller skates.
The 90-minute show, which kicked off the new season last night at the Theatre, is a grand little piece of smart dumb fun.
Witness “Xanadu,” the outlandishly enjoyable stage spoof of the outrageously bad movie from 1980 about a painter and his muse who find love at a roller disco in Los Angeles.
This supremely silly musical adaptation of the 1980. Olivia Newton-John movie is a fizzy concoction that's as sweet and insubstantial as cotton candy.

It often seems as though the show will implode long before the integral paper streamers and cavalcades of mirrored balls have come and gone, but through sheer force of will the musical becomes what the movie couldn't: a delightful, smile-forcing summer night out.
Have to believe she is magic: Olivia Newton-John joined the curtain call last night at the opening of "Xanadu," Broadway's version of her 1980 camp classic.
At a mere 90 minutes the evening still seemed over long with little but the marvelous tongue in check performances to sustain it.
